channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: Hammock's future Modern Mexx restaurant to be moved to northeast corner of lot
item.description: Modern Mexx will replace the Fusion 386 restaurant on S.R. A1A. Flagler Planning Board member Thomas Connor said that though the setbacks do not meet LDC requirements, they are still an improvement.

item.title: Flagler County, Flagler Beach work to avoid lawsuit over Summertown
item.description: Four of five dispute issues resolved as officials work to protect floodplain land and prevent court action

item.title: ICI Homes' Palm Coast development to be donated for local essential workers
item.description: The Palm Coast City Council approved an application to increase the E Section development to 71 homes from 58, contingent on the property going toward affordable, quality homes for essential workers.

item.title: 500-home development with shopping center at Seminole Woods OK'd by Flagler planning board
item.description: In the 'worst-case' scenario analyzed by county staff, the development would be approved for a maximum of 502 homes and almost 830,000 square feet of commercial space.

item.title: No decorative banding: Ormond Beach to pursue standard sidewalks for downtown
item.description: The city is aiming to build sidewalks that are in line with FDOT's standards. As a result, the state department will take over their maintenance and liability.

item.title: Volusia County Council turns down local 'toilet to tap' ban, charter amendment in 4-3 vote
item.description: Citing no county plans to reuse blackwater into drinking water, and with control over only 7% of utilities, the majority of the council voted against an ordinance or 2026 charter amendment.

item.title: Flagler County eyes 21-acre property in The Hammock to environmentally sensitive land program
item.description: Cedar Point is located on the eastern edge of the Intracoastal Waterway, 0.33 miles south of the River to Sea Preserve. It is owned by the DuPont family and has the family cemetery on site.

item.title: Young hero: Ormond Beach boy receives life saving award for helping family to safety during house fire
item.description: Six-year-old Austin, who is in kindergarten, helped wake his family up during a Feb. 2 house fire. On Feb. 10, the Ormond Beach Fire Department recognized him wit a life saving award.

item.title: Salty Church brews up community with grand opening of The Boardroom
item.description: Grand opening draws locals for first taste of waffles, specialty coffee and a new space designed for connection

item.title: Tomoka Christian Church welcomes hundreds for 2026 Night to Shine celebration
item.description: More than 600 volunteers, 480 VIP guests and nearly 800 parents and caregivers took part in the global event sponsored by the Tim Tebow Foundation in Ormond Beach.
